docs.title: CertMan ( X509 Cert, CRL Manager )
docs.text:
This program is a management program that generates X.509 certificates, CRLs, CSRs and key pairs.

Supported algorithms are RSA and ECDSA algorithms. The file can be downloaded from this page link (size is about 30M) This is a program I made personally, so if you have any questions or bugs, please Use Google Groups

[Download] CertMan Version 2.3.4 (Win64)

[Download] CertMan Version 2.3.4 (MacOS)

[Download] CertMan Version 2.3.4 (Linux64)

If you would like to receive a license, simply write a request in Free License Request and you can receive a trial (30-day) license. Of course, you can apply for a license multiple times.

This is a Manual link to the Korean manual page. Although it is lacking, the manual page supports a translator.

docs.title: CertMan Menu Manual
docs.text:
This manual describes the menus implemented by the CertMan main window, using both the application screenshot and the menu/action definitions in src/CertMan/mainwindow.cpp and src/CertMan/mainwindow2.cpp.

The screenshot shows File, View, Tools, Data, Service, and Help. The Server menu is added in the Pro edition, so it does not appear in this screenshot. Menu availability also depends on the active license. Toolbar visibility can be customized from View.

docs.title: File
docs.text: Menu item Shortcut Description New Ctrl+N Create a new database. Open... Ctrl+O Open an existing database. Remote Database Ctrl+R Connect to a remote database. Logout Ctrl+T Disconnect from the current database. Recent Files — Reopen a recently used database. Up to ten entries are maintained. Quit Ctrl+Q Exit CertMan.

docs.title: View
docs.text:
The View menu is available when a license is active. Its submenus contain checkable items for showing or hiding individual toolbar buttons:

  • File ToolBar: New, Open, Remote Database, and Logout.
  • Tool ToolBar: key generation, request and user creation, certificate and CRL profile creation, certificate/CRL creation, revocation, and the CA/Profile managers. Pro editions also include Make Config and Register Signer.
  • Data ToolBar: Import Data, Get data from URI, Publish to LDAP, Set Passwd, and Change Passwd. Pro editions also include TSP Client.
  • Server ToolBar (Pro): OCSP, TSP, CMP, REG, CC, and KMS server controls.
  • Service ToolBar: TSP, OCSP, CA, and ACME service controls.
  • Help ToolBar: Settings, Clear Log, Log, and About CertMan. Pro editions also include Server Status.
  • Set Default: restore the default toolbar visibility settings. The application may ask to restart to apply toolbar changes.

These controls affect toolbar visibility; the corresponding commands remain available from their main menus.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Menu item Shortcut Description New keypair Shift+F1 Generate a new public/private key pair. Make Request Shift+F2 Create a certificate signing request (CSR). Register User Shift+F4 Register a user. Make Config (Pro) Shift+F3 Generate configuration information. Register Signer (Pro) Shift+F5 Register a signer. Make Cert Profile Shift+F6 Create a certificate profile. Make CRL Profile Shift+F7 Create a certificate revocation list (CRL) profile. Make Certificate Shift+F8 Create a certificate. Make CRL Shift+F9 Create a CRL. Revoke Certificate Shift+F10 Revoke a certificate. CA Manager Shift+F11 Open the CA management window. Profile Manager Shift+F11 Open the profile management window.

docs.title: Data
docs.text: Menu item Shortcut Description Import data Ctrl+Alt+I Import supported data into the database. Get data from URI Ctrl+Alt+U Retrieve data from a URI. Publish to LDAP Ctrl+Alt+L Publish directory data to LDAP. This command is disabled in the unlicensed version. Set Passwd Ctrl+Alt+P Set a password for a private key. Disabled in the unlicensed version. Change Passwd Ctrl+Alt+C Change a private key password. Disabled in the unlicensed version. TSP Client (Pro) Ctrl+Alt+T Open the Time-Stamp Protocol client tool.

docs.title: Server (Pro)
docs.text:
The Server menu is present in the Pro edition. Each command opens the corresponding server setup or management window.

Menu item Shortcut Description OCSP Server Shift+O Configure an Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) server. TSP Server Shift+T Configure a Time-Stamp Protocol (TSP) server. CMP Server Shift+C Configure a Certificate Management Protocol (CMP) server. REG Server Shift+R Configure the registration server. CC Server Shift+A Configure the CC server. KMS Server Shift+K Configure a Key Management Service (KMS) server.

docs.title: Service
docs.text:
These commands configure or open the corresponding service. Service commands are disabled in the unlicensed version.

Menu item Shortcut Description TSP Service Shift+T Set up the TSP service. OCSP Service Shift+O Set up the OCSP service. CA Service Shift+C Set up the CA service. ACME Service Shift+A Set up the Automatic Certificate Management Environment (ACME) service.

docs.title: Help
docs.text: Menu item Shortcut Description Server Status (Pro) — Show server status information. Settings — Open application settings. Clear Log F9 Clear the log output. Disabled in the unlicensed version. Log F10 Toggle log output. Disabled in the unlicensed version. License Information — View license information. Bug or Issue Report — Open the bug and issue reporting destination. Q and A — Open the question-and-answer destination. About CertMan F1 Show information about CertMan.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Shortcuts use the platform's standard modifier names: Ctrl means Control and Shift means Shift.
  • Some commands require an open database or suitable permissions and may be unavailable until those conditions are met.
  • The source assigns Shift+F11 to both CA Manager and Profile Manager, and uses the same shortcuts for some Server and Service pairs (Shift+O, Shift+T, Shift+C, and Shift+A). Which command responds can depend on the platform's shortcut handling.
  • Menu labels and behavior are based on the main-window implementation in src/CertMan/mainwindow.cpp and src/CertMan/mainwindow2.cpp.

docs.title: Make Request Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the Make request dialog used to create a certificate signing request (CSR). Open it from Tools > Make Request (Shift+F2). A database connection is required.

docs.title: Create a CSR
docs.text:
1. Enter a Name for the request.
  2. Enter the subject DN (Distinguished Name), or click Make DN to compose it with the DN editor.
  3. Optionally enter ChallengePass and UnstructuredName values.
  4. Choose how to provide the signing key:
  5. Keep Generate Key Pair unchecked and use Key Select to choose an existing key pair.
  6. Check Generate Key Pair to create a new key pair in this dialog, then use Key Generate to set its name, algorithm, and parameters.
  7. Optionally check Use Extension and select a CSR profile. Use View to inspect the selected profile.
  8. Choose the Signature Hash when the selected key algorithm supports a separate hash.
  9. Click OK to create and save the CSR. Click Cancel to close without submitting it.

The request name and DN are required. If extensions are enabled, a CSR profile must be selected. If using an existing key, select a key pair first. On success, CertMan saves the request, marks the associated key pair as used, refreshes the Request list, and displays CSR created.

docs.title: Request information
docs.text: Field or control Purpose Name Required name for the CSR record. DN Required subject distinguished name encoded in the request. Make DN Opens the DN editor, retaining the current DN as its starting value. ChallengePass Optional challenge password attribute. UnstructuredName Optional unstructured name attribute. Signature Hash Selects the digest used for the CSR signature when applicable. The initial value comes from the application's default hash setting.

docs.title: Select an existing key pair
docs.text:
When Generate Key Pair is unchecked, the Key Select tab is used:

Field or control Purpose Key Name Read-only name of the selected key pair. Num Read-only database record number for the key pair. Select Opens the CA Manager selection dialog. Choose a key pair and confirm. Key pair description Read-only description of the selected key pair.

The key's algorithm and parameters are taken from the selected database record. For PKCS#11 or KMIP keys, the corresponding configured provider is used to create the CSR signature.

docs.title: Generate a new key pair
docs.text:
Check Generate Key Pair to switch to the Key Generate tab. The existing-key tab becomes unavailable until the checkbox is cleared.

Field or control Purpose Key Name Required database name for the newly generated key pair. CertMan may suggest the request name followed by _keyPair. Mechanism Select RSA, ECDSA, DSA, EdDSA, or SM2. The PQC row contains ML-DSA and SLH-DSA. Public Exponent RSA public exponent, initially 65537; disabled for algorithms that do not use it. Key Length / parameter dropdown Select the mechanism-specific key size, curve, or parameter set. Defaults to RSA 2048 unless changed by a saved key-generation preference. To PKCS#11 Generate the key through a configured PKCS#11 token/HSM when supported and available. To KMIP Generate through KMIP. This control is shown in Pro and depends on the configured KMIP provider.

The available key parameters follow the choices in the New keypair dialog: RSA sizes 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096, and 8192; DSA sizes 1024, 2048, and 3072; supported named curves for ECDSA; Ed25519/Ed448; SM2; ML-DSA-44/65/87; and the SLH-DSA SHA2/SHAKE parameter sets. Exact availability can depend on the selected storage provider and edition.

docs.title: CSR profile and extensions
docs.text:
• Use Extension enables the CSR profile controls.
  • CSR Profile displays the selected profile name and record number. Click Select to choose a profile; click View to inspect it.
  • The Set to default checkbox beside the extension controls saves the extension/profile selection for later use. The last selection is restored when the dialog is opened again.
  • When a profile includes Subject Key Identifier or Authority Key Identifier extensions, CertMan derives the key identifier from the public key while building the request.

docs.title: Signature hash behavior
docs.text: The hash dropdown is disabled for EdDSA, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA, whose signature algorithms determine the digest behavior. Selecting SM2 sets the hash to SM3. When an existing key pair is selected, the dialog adjusts hash availability based on that key.

docs.title: Edition and configuration notes
docs.text:
• In the unlicensed version, RSA is selected and the other mechanism choices are disabled.
  • To PKCS#11 is disabled when the PKCS#11 context is unavailable. PKCS#11 use also requires valid settings and an accessible session.
  • To KMIP is hidden outside Pro. It requires KMIP configuration.
  • Some algorithm/storage combinations are restricted by the dialog. For example, PKCS#11 selection disables SM2 and the PQC mechanisms in the key-generation controls.
  • For internally stored keys, CertMan uses its private-key password feature when that feature is enabled.

docs.title: Related implementation
docs.text: This guide is based on images/make_req_dlg.png, src/CertMan/make_req_dlg.ui, src/CertMan/make_req_dlg.h, src/CertMan/make_req_dlg.cpp, and the Tools > Make Request action in src/CertMan/mainwindow.cpp.

docs.title: New Key Pair Dialog Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the New keypair dialog in CertMan. The dialog is opened from Tools > New keypair (shortcut: Shift+F1). A database must be connected before you can open it.

docs.title: Create a key pair
docs.text:
1. Enter a unique, recognizable value in Name. The name is required.
  2. Select a Mechanism. Choose one of the standard algorithms, or a post-quantum algorithm in the PQC row.
  3. Select the parameter or key length from the dropdown. The available choices depend on the selected mechanism.
  4. For RSA, review or change Exponent. It defaults to 65537. This field is disabled for algorithms that do not use an RSA exponent.
  5. Optionally select a key storage destination, if available and configured.
  6. Select Set to default if you want this algorithm and parameter selection to be preselected the next time the dialog opens.
  7. Click OK to generate and save the key pair. Click Close to leave without generating it.

After successful generation, CertMan stores the key pair in the connected database, refreshes the KeyPair list, and reports Key pair generated. If generation fails, the dialog displays an error.

docs.title: Fields and options
docs.text: Control Purpose Name Database name for the key pair. It cannot be empty. Mechanism Select RSA, ECDSA, DSA, EdDSA, or SM2. PQC Select ML-DSA or SLH-DSA, the post-quantum algorithm choices. Key Length / parameter dropdown Choose the algorithm-specific size, curve, or parameter set. The label changes to match the selected algorithm. Exponent RSA public exponent; the initial value is 65537. To PKCS#11 Generate using a configured PKCS#11 token or HSM. This option is unavailable if the PKCS#11 provider is not loaded. To KMIP Generate through KMIP. This option is shown in Pro and requires suitable KMIP configuration. Set to default Save the selected algorithm, parameter, and HSM choice as the dialog's next default. OK Generate and save the key pair. Close Close the dialog without submitting the form.

docs.title: Algorithm parameters
docs.text:
The parameter dropdown is populated for the selected mechanism:

Mechanism Choices provided by the application RSA Key sizes: 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096, or 8192 bits. ECDSA Named elliptic curves, including prime256v1, secp256k1, secp384r1, and secp521r1. The full list is available in the dropdown. DSA Key sizes: 1024, 2048, or 3072 bits. EdDSA Ed25519 or Ed448. SM2 SM2 parameter. ML-DSA ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, or ML-DSA-87. SLH-DSA SHA2 or SHAKE parameter sets at 128-, 192-, or 256-bit security levels, with s and f variants.

docs.title: Availability and storage notes
docs.text:
• The unlicensed version selects RSA and disables the other mechanism choices.
  • The To PKCS#11 option is enabled only when the PKCS#11 context is available. PKCS#11 settings and a usable token/session are also required when generating.
  • To KMIP appears in Pro. KMIP supports the mechanisms implemented by the application; some mechanism choices are disabled while KMIP is selected.
  • ML-DSA and SLH-DSA use the application's software key generation path even if PKCS#11 is selected; they are not generated as PKCS#11 keys by this dialog implementation.
  • Key generation requires a connected database. Internal private keys are encrypted when CertMan's private-key password feature is enabled.
